mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (measured as month-over-month change) signals monetary tightening, which compresses equity valuations by raising discount rates for future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increased by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE falls below 4.5%, the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in residential construction permits (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust household demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS increase by at least 1% over the prior month, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve's response of raising the federal funds rate compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and FEDFUNDS rises, the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the regime-conditional signal is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals expanding labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% over the prior month, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1900 thousand units signals weakening residential demand that reduces construction sector activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST falls below 1900, the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of such instances, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening economy that reduces corporate profit expectations, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls by at least 0.5% and UNRATE rises by at least 0.2 percentage points over the prior month, the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is negative over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer spending (RSAFS > 360,000 million dollars), the resulting economic expansion drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS exceeds 360,000 million dollars, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances, or the Rank IC over any 2-year rolling window is below 0.03.
